title: The Revolution, March 1821
text: Mani rises on 29 March 1821. Within weeks the Peloponnese, Roumeli and the islands are in revolt.

title: Tripolitsa falls, 5 October 1821
text: The capital of the Morea is stormed after a five-month siege. Black rings: fortresses still held by the Ottomans.

title: Maniaki, 1 June 1825
text: Ibrahim Pasha's Egyptian army defeats Papaflessas. Messenia falls, and by the end of 1825 most of the Morea.

title: The Exodus of Missolonghi, 22–23 April 1826
text: After a year's siege the defenders break out; few survive. Western Roumeli is lost, and Athens falls in August.

title: Navarino, 20 October 1827
text: British, French and Russian squadrons destroy the Ottoman–Egyptian fleet. A French army lands in 1828 and Ibrahim leaves the Morea.

title: Petra, 24 September 1829
text: The last battle of the war: the Ottoman force capitulates and leaves eastern Roumeli.

title: The London Protocol, 3 February 1830
text: Britain, France and Russia declare Greece independent, within a smaller line, from the Achelous to the Spercheios (dashed).

title: The Kingdom of Greece, 1832
text: The Arta–Volos line is agreed with the Porte. Athens, Euboea and Lamia are handed over in 1833.

title: The risings of 1854
text: During the Crimean War, bands led by Greek officers rise in Epirus, Thessaly and Macedonia (orange). Britain and France occupy Piraeus (1854–57).

title: The Ionian Islands, 2 June 1864
text: Britain gives up its protectorate, and the Ionian Islands join Greece.

title: Thessaly and Arta, 1881
text: After the Berlin Conference, the Convention of Constantinople cedes Thessaly and the Arta district.

title: Domokos, 17 May 1897
text: The Army is beaten. Thessaly stays under Ottoman occupation until 1898, and Greece cedes small border strips (not drawn).

title: The Cretan State, December 1898
text: Crete becomes autonomous, with Prince George of Greece as High Commissioner. Samos has been a principality since 1834.

title: Sarantaporo, 22–23 October 1912
text: The First Balkan War. The Army forces the pass into Macedonia; Thessaloniki surrenders on 8 November, and the fleet takes the islands.

title: Bizani, 5–6 March 1913
text: The fortress line falls and Ioannina surrenders; the Army moves on into Northern Epirus.

title: Kresna Gorge, 21–31 July 1913
text: The Second Balkan War ends. The Treaty of Bucharest (10 August) fixes the border on the Nestos.

title: Crete and Epirus, 1913
text: Crete is united with Greece; the Treaty of Athens with the Ottoman Empire confirms Epirus and Macedonia.

title: The islands and Northern Epirus, 1914
text: The Powers award the eastern Aegean islands to Greece and Northern Epirus to Albania. The Greek Army withdraws; the Epirotes declare autonomy.

title: The occupation of Eastern Macedonia, 1916
text: During the National Schism, Bulgarian and German troops occupy the land east of the Strymon, until October 1918.

title: Smyrna, 15 May 1919
text: The Greek Army lands with Allied approval, and within weeks holds the coast and the valleys inland.

title: The summer offensive, 1920
text: The Army reaches Prusa, Uşak and the Sea of Marmara, and occupies Eastern Thrace.

title: The Treaty of Sèvres, 10 August 1920
text: Eastern Thrace, Imbros and Tenedos are awarded to Greece, and the Smyrna zone (dashed) goes under Greek administration. It is never ratified.

title: The Sakarya, 23 August – 13 September 1921
text: The offensive fails less than 100 km from Ankara, and the Army falls back to the Eskişehir–Afyon Karahisar line.

title: Dumlupınar, 26–30 August 1922
text: The front breaks. Within three weeks the Army has left Asia Minor, and Smyrna burns.

title: Mudanya, October 1922
text: Greece agrees to leave Eastern Thrace, and the Army withdraws behind the Evros.

title: The Treaty of Lausanne, 24 July 1923
text: Eastern Thrace, Imbros and Tenedos go to Turkey; Western Thrace and the eastern Aegean islands stay Greek.

title: Corfu, August–September 1923
text: Italy occupies the island for four weeks after an Italian general is murdered on the Albanian border.

title: 28 October 1940
text: Italy invades from Albania. In the Pindus and on the Kalamas the attack is held and thrown back; by December the Army holds a quarter of Albania.

title: Rupel, 6–9 April 1941
text: Germany attacks from Bulgaria. The forts hold, but are outflanked through Yugoslavia; Athens falls on 27 April.

title: Crete, 20 May – 1 June 1941
text: German paratroops land at Maleme. The island falls, and the occupation of Greece is complete.

title: The Triple Occupation, 1941–44
text: German, Italian and Bulgarian zones; Bulgaria annexes most of Eastern Macedonia and Western Thrace.

title: Liberation, October 1944
text: The Germans leave Athens on 12 October; Western Crete and Milos hold out until May 1945.

title: The Dodecanese, 1947
text: Italy cedes the islands by the Treaty of Paris. Greece takes over on 31 March 1947.

title: Vitsi and Grammos, August 1949
text: The National Army takes the Democratic Army's last bases on the Albanian border; the civil war ends.

title: Today
text: 131,957 km². The borders have not changed since 1947. Faintly drawn: the lands once held or awarded and lost.
